records.current_scope:
Let H_n(z;q)=sum_k [n choose k]_q z^k, D_n(q)=Disc_z H_n, n=Ad+b, d odd, ω primitive of order d, and q(ε)=ω(1+ε²)^(1/d). Put F=z^d+1 and P_A=product_(j=1)^A j^j.
Separated case: G=H_b(z;ω), 0≤b<d, A≥1, Disc(G)Res(F,G)≠0. At α^d=−1, H_n(α+εx;q(ε))=ε^A(−1)^A d^(A/2)G(α)He_A(√d x/α)+O(ε^(A+1)). With K=dA(A−1)/2, D_n(q(ε))=ε^(2K)(C+O(ε²)), C=(−1)^(A(d−1)/2)d^(dA(A+1)/2)P_A^d Disc(G)Res(F,G)^(2A). Thus ord_(Φ_d)D_n=K.
Simple-overlap case: d≥3, b odd with 1≤b<d. Write G=(z+1)U, g=U(−1), W=(ω;ω)_b/(ω²;ω²)_((b+d)/2), τ=dW/g and J_(A+1)=He_(A+1)+A(1−τ)He_(A−1). If g≠0, H_n(−1+εx;q(ε))=ε^(A+1)(−1)^(A+1)d^((A−1)/2)g J_(A+1)(−√d x;τ)+O(ε^(A+2)).
If additionally Disc(U)Res(F,U)Disc(J_(A+1))≠0, L=dA(A−1)/2+A and D_n(q(ε))=ε^(2L)(C+O(ε²)), C=(−1)^(A(d−1)/2)d^(dA(A+1)/2+A)P_A^(d−1)Disc(J_(A+1))Disc(U)Res(F,U)^(2A)g². Hence ord_(Φ_d)D_n=L. Square roots cancel coefficientwise.

proof_status_evidence.text: Independent bounded recurrence ACCEPT: N=2^w, f(w)=C(N)/N, nonnegative finite bases and coefficients, fixed kappa>=0 and one consistently charged ledger satisfying f(w)<=rho(w)[f(floor(w/2))+f(ceil(w/2))]+kappa eventually. A fixed eventual rho(w)<=r gives C(N)=O(N(log N)^log2(2r)) for 1/2<r<1, O(N log log N) at r=1/2 and O(N) for 0<=r<1/2. An eventual rate rho(w)<=r_*+c/w^gamma with fixed c>=0,gamma>0 and 0<=r_*<1 preserves the corresponding limiting exponent/endpoints. Mere convergence to 1/2 is insufficient: with d(w)=ceil(log2 w), rho(w)=(d+1)/(2d), kappa=f(1)=1, the equality solution at w=2^j is (j+1)H_(j+1), not O(j). These are recurrence statements, not Fourier complexity lower bounds or realized savings.

[2026-10-10 12:40 UTC; reviewed scoped update] Scoped extension linked to the existing inverse-support floor, not a claim that the new source and historical theorem are identical. For normalized complex DFT U, invertible M and M^-1=B+E with rank(E)<=r, |I|=t>r, J the union of B-row supports and d=t-r, ||M-U||_2^2 >= 1-sigma_d(U[J,I])^2 >= max(0,1-t|J|/[N(t-r)]). The singular-value statement holds for every unitary U; the explicit Frobenius bound uses Fourier flatness. Scalar row-sparsity bounds require integer 1<=s<=N: r=0 gives sqrt(1-s/N); r>=1 gives sqrt(max(0,1-4sr/N)). For s=0, invertibility forces full-rank defect and the universal error lower bound is zero. Independently accepted refinements use the local forbidden-block rank rho=rank(E[I,J^c]); give the exact optimum/infimum for one prescribed allowed neighborhood B[I,J^c]=0 with unrestricted remaining entries; and correct the positive-integer-rank scalar formulations to equivalence. For the nonempty one-neighborhood regime 1<=d<=min(t,|J|), a positive critical singular value gives attainment; at zero the infimum is one but every feasible invertible M has error >1.
